title: Introduce cohort reweighting and batch-aware thresholds CI hook for prompt-set regressions
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Small prompt cohorts and variable batch sizes can mask real regressions or generate spurious failures in CI. This PR implements a CI hook that computes per-cohort effective sample size (ESS), applies a cohort reweighting scheme, and adapts metric thresholds based on the batch distribution observed in CI runs. The design goals are: 1) reduce noisy false positives from low-sample cohorts, 2) surface regressions that matter to overall production-weighted metrics, and 3) keep CI deterministic and fast. Changes: added a new hook `cohort_reweight_and_batch_threshold` that runs as part of the eval-harness CI pipeline. The hook performs: a) per-cohort ESS calculation using bootstrap variance estimates, b) weight assignment proportional to ESS with a floor/ceiling to prevent domination by one cohort, c) batch-aware threshold scaling — thresholds are loosened/tightened based on the observed median batch size and variance during the job, d) a noise-aware z-score calibration to convert small-sample deviations into calibrated p-values, and e) deterministic resampling with a seed derived from job id to keep reruns reproducible. The hook emits a short summary artifact (JSON) and a human-readable diff that can be posted on the PR. Implementation notes: - New module: eval_harness/ci_hooks/cohort_reweighting.py (core logic, unit-tested) - New integration: eval_harness/ci_integrations/github_actions_cohort.yml to wire the hook into the existing GH Actions eval job - CLI flag: --cohort-reweight-config to allow local dev runs with custom floors/ceilings - Backwards compatibility: when the hook is disabled, the pipeline falls back to the previous single-threshold gate. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for ESS and weight assignment with synthetic cohorts - End-to-end integration test that runs a small prompt-set with controlled batch distributions - Baseline run included in the PR artifacts showing stable behavior on internal benchmark models - Stress test on large cohort matrix that verifies runtime stays within CI quota Known limitations and future work: - Current weight scheme is linear in ESS; future work will experiment with entropy-regularized weights - Does not yet cross-check with historical drift detect hooks (planned follow-up) - Might require threshold tuning per-model family for very imbalanced prompt sets Checklist: - [x] Implementation + unit tests - [x] Integration into GH Actions - [x] Lightweight artifact emitter for PR comments - [x] Documentation for on-call and SRE teams - [x] Linear tickets linked for rollout and post-mortem Observability and ops: The hook emits the following metrics to the eval-harness metrics namespace: cohort_count, cohort_ess_median, cohort_weight_entropy, threshold_scale_factor. The summary artifact includes per-cohort before/after weights, ESS, and alert decisions. Rollout: feature flag controlled via org config; default enabled for non-critical branches and enabled by policy for release branches after one successful week on main. See linked linear tickets for rollout schedule and verification steps.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can you confirm that ESS floor of 5 is safe for our smallest prompt-sets? We should avoid hiding regressions from critical cohorts.
Maya Patel: Responded: We set a conservative floor of 5 and added a safety alert when a critical cohort falls below the floor — see unit tests and artifact outputs.
Sofia Ramirez: Suggestion: make the threshold_scale_factor clamped between 0.75 and 1.25 to avoid overly permissive changes in large variance jobs.
Maya Patel: Applied Sofia's clamp and added an integration test demonstrating behavior at the clamp extremes.
Arjun Mehta: Approval after one nit on logging formatting.
CI: Integration tests took 9m; one flaky test (test_resample_determinism) reran and passed.
Release Engineering: Please flag if we need a docs-only change for internal runbooks.
merge_outcome: Merged after approvals and passing CI; no post-merge fixes required
release_notes: Added a CI hook to reweight small cohorts and adapt thresholds by batch distribution to reduce noisy eval failures. This is feature-gated and can be turned off via org config.
